body:
It looks to me that 1.1.4 and 1.1.5 and not necessary and can be deleted. We already cover threat modeling in 1.1.2

1.1.2 | Verify the use of threat modeling for every design change or sprint planning to identify threats, plan for countermeasures, facilitate appropriate risk responses, and guide security testing. |   | ✓ | ✓ | 1053
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --

And here is the current status of 1.1.4 and 1.1.5

1.1.4 | Verify documentation and justification of all the application's trust boundaries, components, and significant data flows. |   | ✓ | ✓ | 1059
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
1.1.5 | Verify definition and security analysis of the application's high-level architecture and all connected remote services. (C1) |   | ✓ | ✓ | 1059

1.1.4	Verify documentation and justification of all the application's trust boundaries, components, and significant data flows.		✓	✓	1059
1.1.5	Verify definition and security analysis of the application's high-level architecture and all connected remote services. ([C1](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))		✓	✓	1059

comments.body:
1.1.5 is explored in #1227.  I don't think it is threat modeling but rather it's purpose is to document how interactions with external systems are secured. We can discuss that further there if necessary.

I would like to explore 1.1.4 in detail and I take that as a task for myself.

However, I would point out that in ASVS we should not be mandating activities such as threat modeling, That should be covered by OpenSAMM. We should however be mandating documentation artefacts that are critical to being able to secure the application or describe it's security mechanisms.
Dropping this into the V1 rework bucket

I think 1.1.2 is just TM process and will be removed (or modified) by #1227.

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **1.1.4** | Verify documentation and justification of all the application's trust boundaries, components, and significant data flows. | | ✓ | ✓ | 1059 |
| **1.1.5** | Verify definition and security analysis of the application's high-level architecture and all connected remote services. ([C1](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering)) | | ✓ | ✓ | 1059 |

[CWE-1059](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1059.html) for both is "CWE-1059: Insufficient Technical Documentation"

So the goal here should be: to analyze, are those mentioned and previously required documentation required as pre-conditions for implementing and testing some other section or requirement in ASVS.

If not, we can just delete the requirement as out of scope.

If it is, then we can modify it to be more clear of the expected outcome and move to a more precise section.

Personally, I can not find any good and quick match for 1.1.4.

  * "application's trust boundaries" - ?
  * "components" - covered by "V14.2.5 Verify that a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is maintained of all third party libraries in use."
  * "significant data flows" - ?

For 1.1.5 
* "for connected remote services" - I have proposed to have a separate documentation requirement in #1541. Maybe we can handle those together. 
* "application's high-level architecture" - ?

Recommend merging to:

> Verify that an architecture document exists which demonstrates the application's components, trust boundary assumptions, significant data flows, and remote 3rd party services which it relies upon.
Changed my mind because we also have #1184 to consider
This is why the "rework" category exists so that we can consider a chapter as a whole rather than making a change and then discovering we need to make another change 🙃

> Verify that an architecture document exists which demonstrates the application's components, trust boundary assumptions, significant data flows, and remote 3rd party services which it relies upon.

In practice, it is something you need to do, but for ASVS - what is the expected outcome for this requirement for the verification? For me it is not clear, what I should do with this requirement as a pen-tester.

> > Verify that an architecture document exists which demonstrates the application's components, trust boundary assumptions, significant data flows, and remote 3rd party services which it relies upon.
> 
> In practice, it is something you need to do, but for ASVS - what is the expected outcome for this requirement for the verification? For me it is not clear, what I should do with this requirement as a pen-tester.

While I agree with Elar's point mostly, I do think the usual solution is either a security architecture document or in many cases an application diagram that clearly shows the different components would suffice to verify this.

1.1.5 part "Verify definition ~~and security analysis of the application's high-level architecture and~~ all connected remote services.	" can be documentation requirement for V13 API and Web Service or also for V14 Configuration.

related: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/993

ping @tghosth , please re-check the issue and what is your vision or idea with this now. I think we have a bit more clear scope and understanding, what kind of requirements we want to the ASVS.

The "need for external communications" documentation requirement should be viewed separately via #993, so mainly we should analyze, what we need from 1.1.4 and the first part of 1.1.5 as already pointed out in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1541#issuecomment-1843182931
1.1.5 is being handled elsewhere, I don't think that 1.1.4 satisfies the "without it your app is insecure" test.
So the proposal is to delete 1.1.4 as out of scope, pure documentation requirement without a clear security decision to provide as a pre-condition for other requirements.
I agree on deleting 1.1.4 per the OP.
